page: Microsoft Azure ND96isr_H100_v5 is an isolated, GPU-accelerated server instance designed for high-performance artificial intelligence and parallel compute workloads. The system is equipped with 96 dedicated Intel x86_64 vCPUs running on Microsoft Hyper-V, paired with 1,900 GB of system memory, providing approximately 19.79 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Hardware acceleration is anchored by eight NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs with a collective 640 GB of VRAM. High-speed local scratch capacity is delivered through 31,820 GB of bundled NVMe SSD storage. The platform is also RDMA capable to support multi-node interconnectivity and is compatible with Azure Premium Storage.

The combination of eight flagship accelerators, large system memory, and tens of terabytes of local NVMe storage creates an enterprise-grade profile that minimizes data transfer bottlenecks. Tradeoffs include managing the ephemeral nature of the local NVMe disks and provisioning external networking, as zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

The hardware configuration is targeted at distributed large language model training, multi-GPU neural network inference, large-scale deep learning research, and high-performance scientific simulations.
description: Microsoft Azure ND96isr_H100_v5 is an isolated GPU-accelerated virtual machine built for large-scale deep learning and scientific computing. It features 96 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs running on Intel processors via Microsoft Hyper-V, accompanied by 1,900 GB of system memory. Hardware acceleration is driven by eight NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs providing an aggregate of 640 GB of GPU memory. The instance includes 31,820 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, along with RDMA networking capability and Premium Storage compatibility. With massive memory capacity per core and immense accelerator throughput, the server caters to compute and memory-intensive applications. It operates without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating configured networking for inbound connectivity. This hardware footprint is engineered for distributed large language model training, transformer model fine-tuning, high-throughput deep learning inference, and complex parallel scientific simulations.
